title: Option registration, deferred options and argparse generation
answers: How do addon/script options become settable from CLI --set or config?
How does cmdline.py build argparse flags from options?
body:
Both paths end in `optmanager.py:OptManager.add_option` (stores `_Option`, fires `changed`). Core: `options.py:Options.__init__`. Addons: `load(self, loader)` → `addonmanager.py:Loader.add_option` (no-op if identical signature exists; differing signature → warning + override).
`AddonManager.register` builds Loader, fires LoadHook, fills lookup/commands, then calls `options.process_deferred()`, which applies deferred --set/config values (parsed by `_parse_setval`) once their option exists. Unknown options are stashed in `OptManager.deferred` (via `set(..., defer=True)`).
CLI flags: `tools/cmdline.py:common_options/mitmproxy/mitmdump/mitmweb` call `opts.make_parser(parser, name, metavar=, short=)` (`OptManager.make_parser`): skips unregistered options, bool → `--x/--no-x`, Sequence[str] → append, `dest=optname` (so `vars(args)` keys match option names), defaults None so config file isn't overridden.
